tools.name: whoami

findings.detail: Description of "whoami" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: whoami, get_news · Private data: get_balance, get_funding_status, deposit_to_subaccount, top_up_gas · Public sink: top_up_gas, place_limit_order, place_market_order, cancel_order, open_position, get_news, get_referral_program · Destructive: close_position, close_all_positions.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: whoami, get_news · Private data: get_balance, get_funding_status, deposit_to_subaccount, top_up_gas · Public sink: top_up_gas, place_limit_order, place_market_order, cancel_order, open_position, get_news, get_referral_program · Destructive: close_position, close_all_positions

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "whoami" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Report what this session controls: the master account/subaccount, whether it can trade or is read-only, and the exact on-chain authorization scope (which messages, which subaccount, and that it CANNOT withdraw/transfer). Call this first." → after: "Report what this session controls: the master account (its address in BOTH forms — cosmos rit1… and EVM 0x…, the same 20 bytes), the subaccount, whether it can trade or is read-only, and the exact on-chain authorization scope (which messages, which subaccount, and that it CANNOT withdraw/transfer). "

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
